CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone with pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with left-sided back pain that began three days ago. Pain is constant and has been radiating lower toward the groin. Patient has been unable to pass the stone and reports severe pain. She started seeing blood in her urine this morning and is able to urinate. She denies fever but reports chills and nausea. She is unable to eat due to pain level. This is her third episode of kidney stones; prior episodes typically resolved in 3-4 days. She has tried Tylenol and ibuprofen without adequate pain relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports chills and nausea. She denies fever, chest pain, or abdominal pain. Back pain is radiating into the groin.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes
Recurrent kidney stones (third episode)
Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (known)

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily
Tylenol as needed
Ibuprofen as needed

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports difficulty with diet control, particularly high salt and french fry intake. She has obtained a home blood pressure cuff and has been taking readings at least three times per week, with systolic readings ranging from 130s to 150s and diastolic 70-80.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur
Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes
Abdomen: Tenderness to palpation without rebound or guarding
Costovertebral angle: Tenderness on right flank

RESULTS
Home blood glucose readings: Low 100s before meals
Previous glucose test (couple months ago): 300
Previous A1C: 7.3

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Suspected kidney stone with right-sided costovertebral angle tenderness suggestive of renal inflammation. Plan: 1) Prescribe oxycodone 5 mg every 6-8 hours as needed for pain; 2) Continue Tylenol for breakthrough pain; 3) Increase fluid intake to promote stone passage; 4) Provide urine strainer to capture stone if passed; 5) Refer to urology for recurrent kidney stones; 6) Continue Norvasc 2.5 mg for hypertension; 7) Continue Metformin 500 mg for diabetes; 8) Refer to dietitian for dietary counseling and management.
